## Problem

The `HEALTHCHECK` uses shell form (`CMD wget -qO- ... || exit 1`). hadolint 2.15 reports DL3025 for it. `hadolint/hadolint-action` runs with `failure-threshold: info`, so any warning fails the step; `lint` is the root of `needs: lint -> verify -> build -> merge -> update_description`, so a red `lint` blocks every publish path.

The pinned `hadolint-action@2332a7b` (v3.3.0) ships hadolint 2.14.0, which does not fire the rule — that is the only reason `main` is green. v3.4.0 ships 2.15.0 and does fire it, so the repository is pinned to a linter it can no longer upgrade.

## Evidence

Dockerfile:113-114 —

    HEALTHCHECK --interval=60s --timeout=5s --start-period=120s \
      CMD wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/2/summary >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1

Local hadolint 2.15.1 on this exact file:

    Dockerfile:113 DL3025 warning: Use arguments JSON notation for CMD and ENTRYPOINT arguments
    exit=1

The Renovate PR that bumps the action is already red — GitHub Actions run 31063863003 (`renovate/hadolint-hadolint-action-3.x`, 2026-08-06, failure in 15s):

    ##[error]Dockerfile:113 DL3025 warning: Use arguments JSON notation for CMD and ENTRYPOINT arguments

Action-to-linter mapping, from each tag's own Dockerfile:
  hadolint-action v3.3.0 -> ghcr.io/hadolint/hadolint:v2.14.0-debian
  hadolint-action v3.4.0 -> ghcr.io/hadolint/hadolint:v2.15.0-debian

Minimal repro confirming exec form clears it:

    HEALTHCHECK CMD wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/ >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1   -> DL3025, exit 1
    HEALTHCHECK CMD ["wget","-q","http://127.0.0.1:8080/"]                       -> clean, exit 0

## Impact

The Renovate PR for `hadolint-action` sits permanently red and cannot merge. The repository is frozen on hadolint 2.14.0 — it stops receiving new Dockerfile lint rules, which is the opposite of what pinning-plus-Renovate is set up to achieve here. If the pin is ever bumped by hand or the `v3` floating tag is used, `lint` goes red on `main` and no tag can be released until the Dockerfile is edited.

## Fix

Switch the healthcheck to exec form. `wget` already exits non-zero on a failed request, so the `|| exit 1` the shell form needs is redundant, and exec form removes the `sh -c` process per check:

    HEALTHCHECK --interval=60s --timeout=5s --start-period=120s \
      CMD ["wget", "-q", "-O", "/dev/null", "http://127.0.0.1:8080/2/summary"]

`/dev/null` is a device node, so this still works under `--read-only`.

Then keep `.github/workflows/build.yaml`'s "the container's own HEALTHCHECK command, run verbatim" step actually verbatim by reading it out of the image instead of restating it:

    docker inspect -f '{{json .Config.Healthcheck.Test}}' xmrig:ci

and exec'ing the returned argv, or at minimum update the hardcoded `sh -c 'wget -qO- ...'` to match the new form. Do not silence DL3025 in `.hadolint.yaml` — the exec form is the better command here regardless of the linter.

## Resolution
HEALTHCHECK switched to exec form: CMD ["wget","-q","-O","/dev/null","http://127.0.0.1:8080/2/summary"]. hadolint 2.15.1 (the version that was failing the Renovate PR) now exits 0 on this Dockerfile. The build.yaml step that claimed to run the healthcheck "verbatim" no longer restates it — it reads .Config.Healthcheck.Test back out of the image with docker inspect + jq and execs elements 1..n, and errors out if the image declares no healthcheck at all. Verified on a locally built image (xmrig:audit): declared Test is the exact argv, docker reports the container healthy with last probe exitcode=0, and the extracted argv execs successfully inside the running container.
title: Shell-form HEALTHCHECK trips DL3025 on hadolint 2.15, so the lint job that gates the entire release pipeline cannot take its own linter upgrade

## Problem

`livenessProbe` and `readinessProbe` hit `/2/summary` on :8080 but set no `timeoutSeconds`, so both use the Kubernetes default of 1 second. The Dockerfile's `HEALTHCHECK` polls the identical endpoint with `--timeout=5s`. Two consumers of one contract element disagree by 5x, and the stricter one is the one that restarts the pod.

The manifest itself supplies the condition that makes 1s marginal: `limits.cpu: "1"` is a CFS quota, and — as the manifest's own comment states — xmrig reads host topology through hwloc and starts one mining thread per host core regardless. On a large node every one of those threads is contending for a single CPU of quota, and xmrig's HTTP thread is scheduled among them.

## Evidence

deployment.yaml:86-97 —

    livenessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /2/summary
        port: 8080
      initialDelaySeconds: 120
      periodSeconds: 30
    readinessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /2/summary
        port: 8080
      initialDelaySeconds: 30
      periodSeconds: 15

No `timeoutSeconds` on either; Kubernetes defaults it to 1.

Dockerfile:113, same endpoint:

    HEALTHCHECK --interval=60s --timeout=5s --start-period=120s

deployment.yaml:73-79 supplies the contention, in its own words:

    # NOTE: this is a CFS quota, not a CPU set. xmrig reads the host
    # topology via hwloc and cannot see it, so it still starts one
    # mining thread per host core and schedules them all into this one
    # CPU of quota.

docs/audit/arch-profile.md names `:8080` as a contract element consumed jointly by `HEALTHCHECK` and both probes — the exact shape ("two consumers disagreeing with each other") the profile records as the repository's recurring defect.

## Impact

Failing scenario: a 32-core node, `limits.cpu: "1"`, 32 throttled mining threads. Three consecutive liveness probes (default `failureThreshold: 3`, 30s apart) exceed the 1s window while the miner is healthy and hashing. The kubelet restarts the container; RandomX re-initialises its 2080 MiB dataset, taking the pod through another 120s of `initialDelaySeconds`, under the same load. The result is a restart loop of a working miner — and the container's own HEALTHCHECK, which would have tolerated the same latency, reports healthy throughout, so the two signals disagree about the same process.

## Fix

Set `timeoutSeconds` explicitly on both probes to match the value the image already commits to:

    livenessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /2/summary
        port: 8080
      initialDelaySeconds: 120
      periodSeconds: 30
      timeoutSeconds: 5
    readinessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /2/summary
        port: 8080
      initialDelaySeconds: 30
      periodSeconds: 15
      timeoutSeconds: 5

Add the `:8080` probe timeout to the contract row for `:8080` in `docs/audit/arch-profile.md` so the next edit to either side has a stated counterpart.

## Resolution
timeoutSeconds: 5 added to both livenessProbe and readinessProbe, matching the image's HEALTHCHECK --timeout=5s for the same endpoint. Comment states why the 1s default is not survivable under the manifest's own cpu: "1" quota. A contract row for the 5s probe timeout was added to docs/audit/arch-profile.md so the two sides have a stated counterpart. kubeconform -strict validates the edited manifest.
title: Both probes inherit the 1s default timeoutSeconds while the image's own HEALTHCHECK allows 5s for the same endpoint, and the manifest's 1-CPU quota is what makes that 1s miss

## Problem

The step named "Smoke test the image as shipped" starts the container with `docker run -d xmrig:ci` — no `--read-only`, no `--cap-drop ALL`, no `--security-opt no-new-privileges`. Every documented way to run this image applies all three: the README `docker run` recipe, `docker-compose.yml`, and `deployment.yaml` (`readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`, `capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]`, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`).

So the step's own comment — "it runs the image exactly as shipped" — is false in the one dimension that separates a container that starts from a container that starts *for users*. The security posture is asserted in three manifests and executed in none.

## Evidence

.github/workflows/build.yaml:104-110 —

    # `--version` overrides CMD, so the above never reads config.json, never
    # starts the HTTP API and never exercises the HEALTHCHECK. This does: it
    # runs the image exactly as shipped and pins the parts deployment.yaml's
    # probes and the Dockerfile's HEALTHCHECK depend on.
    - name: Smoke test the image as shipped
      run: |
        cid="$(docker run -d xmrig:ci)"

What the three consumers actually apply:

  docker-compose.yml:9-12   read_only: true / cap_drop: ["ALL"] / no-new-privileges:true
  deployment.yaml:43-51     readOnlyRootFilesystem: true / capabilities.drop: ["ALL"] /
                            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  README.md:93              --read-only --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges

docs/audit/arch-profile.md already records the historic instance of this exact shape (`audit-f40795a1`: "same image, three security postures") and lists cross-consumer parity as still unenforced.

## Impact

Failing scenario: an upstream xmrig release, or a future edit to `config.json`, causes the miner to write one file to the root filesystem at startup — a lock file, a cached dataset path, a re-serialised config. CI stays green because CI runs it writable. Every shipped consumer — Compose, Kubernetes, and the README recipe — runs it read-only, so every real deployment fails at start while the release pipeline reports success. The same blind spot covers a future capability requirement: `cap_drop: ALL` is asserted three times and executed zero times.

## Fix

Apply the posture to the container the step already starts — one line, no new step:

    cid="$(docker run -d --read-only --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges xmrig:ci)"

`docker exec` into a read-only container works unchanged, so the `/2/summary` poll, the restricted-mode assertion, and the HEALTHCHECK invocation below it all keep working. Extend the step's comment to say what "as shipped" now covers: the CMD, the config, the API, the healthcheck, *and* the read-only/no-capability posture the three consumers require. Then update the "Cross-consumer parity" bullet in `docs/audit/arch-profile.md` — the security posture moves from unenforced to enforced; memory floor and uid/paths remain.

## Resolution
The "Smoke test the image as shipped" step now starts the container with --read-only --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges, the posture deployment.yaml, docker-compose.yml and the README recipe all assert. Verified end to end against a locally built image rather than assumed: xmrig starts, serves /2/summary, reports "restricted": true, and Docker's own healthcheck loop reaches healthy under all three flags. docs/audit/arch-profile.md's "Current enforcement" section updated — the security posture moves from unenforced to enforced; the memory floor and uid/paths/ownership remain unenforced, and cross-consumer parity of values is now scoped to values only, since schema validation covers well-formedness.
title: The "image as shipped" smoke test runs the container unhardened, so the read-only rootfs and dropped capabilities every documented consumer applies are never executed once in CI

body:
## Problem

`lint` runs hadolint over `Dockerfile` and actionlint over `.github/workflows/`. `docker-compose.yml` and `deployment.yaml` — the two manifests the README instructs users to apply directly — are never opened by any job. A misspelled key, a wrong indent level, or a field that does not exist in the Kubernetes schema ships to `main` and to the release tag with no check.

Kubernetes accepts unknown fields in a manifest silently under client-side apply, so a typo such as `readOnlyRootFileSystem` or `timeoutSecond` does not error at `kubectl apply` — it is dropped, and the pod runs without the setting the manifest appears to declare.

## Evidence

.github/workflows/build.yaml:35-46, the entire lint surface —

    - name: Lint Dockerfile
      uses: hadolint/hadolint-action@2332a7b74a6de0dda2e2221d575162eba76ba5e5 # v3.3.0
      with:
        dockerfile: Dockerfile
    - name: Lint workflows
      uses: docker://rhysd/actionlint@sha256:b1934ee5... # v1.7.12
      with:
        args: -color

`git ls-files` shows `docker-compose.yml` and `deployment.yaml` tracked at the repository root; no job in `build.yaml` references either path.

README.md:116-121 and 175-179 tell users to run them verbatim:

    docker compose up -d
    kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml

`trivy config .` reaches `deployment.yaml` today only because it is run by hand — the `Scan image` step in `verify` uses `image-ref: xmrig:ci`, which scans the built image and not the repository's manifests.

## Impact

Failing scenario: an edit to `deployment.yaml` writes `capabilities.drop` one level too deep, or renames `readOnlyRootFilesystem` by a single character. `kubectl apply` accepts it, the Deployment reconciles, and the pod runs with a writable root filesystem and full default capabilities — the manifest reads as hardened and the cluster is not. The release pipeline is green throughout, because nothing in it ever parsed the file. The equivalent for Compose is a `deploy.resources.limits` key silently ignored, removing the 3 GiB ceiling the file exists to enforce.

## Fix

Add two steps to the `lint` job. Both are schema-aware, which is the point — a plain YAML parse would accept every typo above.

    - name: Validate Compose file
      run: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml config --quiet

    - name: Validate Kubernetes manifests
      uses: docker://ghcr.io/yannh/kubeconform:v0.7.0@sha256:<digest>
      with:
        args: -strict -summary deployment.yaml

`-strict` is what rejects unknown fields; without it kubeconform accepts the misspelling this finding is about. `docker compose config` is already available on `ubuntu-latest` with no extra install. Pin the kubeconform digest the way every other action in this workflow is pinned.

## Resolution
Two steps added to the lint job: `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml config --quiet`, and kubeconform -strict -summary on deployment.yaml, pinned by digest (ghcr.io/yannh/kubeconform@sha256:faffaf43... v0.8.0) like every other action in this workflow. Both proven load-bearing by negative test, not assumed: compose exits 1 on `read_onli:` and on `deploy.resources.limits.memori:`; kubeconform reports deployment.yaml VALID with `readOnlyRootFileSystem` misspelled and only fails it with -strict ("additional properties 'readOnlyRootFileSystem' not allowed", exit 1). Both pass on the real files. The step comments were corrected after testing — an earlier draft claimed compose accepts unknown keys, which it does not.
title: Neither shipped consumer manifest is parsed or schema-checked in CI; the lint job covers only the Dockerfile and the workflows

body:
## Problem

"Persistent logging" tells the reader that if they opt into `"log-file": "/log/xmrig.log"` without adding the volume, "xmrig writes the log inside the container's own filesystem, where it is lost on `--rm` and invisible on the host". The recipe it is amending, in "How to use this image", passes `--read-only`. `/log` in the image is a plain directory on the root filesystem, so under `--read-only` the open fails and no file is created anywhere — the described consequence ("lost on `--rm`") never occurs, because the file the reader is told to expect never exists.

The section itself supplies the reason this matters two paragraphs later: xmrig "writes no file, prints no error, and exits non-zero never". A reader who trusts the stated failure mode goes looking inside the container for a file that was never created and has no error to find.

## Evidence

README.md:315-317 —

    The standalone `docker run` recipe above mounts only `config.json`, so add the
    volume there yourself — without it xmrig writes the log inside the container's
    own filesystem, where it is lost on `--rm` and invisible on the host:

README.md:91-95, the recipe being referred to —

    docker run -dit --rm \
        --cpuset-cpus 0 --memory 3g \
        --read-only --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges \
        --volume "$(pwd)"/config.json:/etc/xmrig/config.json:ro \
        --name xmrig ivuorinen/docker-xmrig:latest

Dockerfile:88-91 — `/log` is an ordinary directory in the image layer, not a volume, so `--read-only` covers it:

    RUN apk --no-cache add libuv hwloc libssl3 && \
      adduser -S -u 10001 -H -h /log xmrig && \
      mkdir -p /etc/xmrig /log && \
      chown 10001 /log

README.md:325-328, the silence this compounds —

    If xmrig cannot open the log file it writes no file, prints no error, and
    exits non-zero never — the feature is simply absent and nothing tells you.

## Impact

A reader following the section verbatim adds `log-file` to `config.json`, restarts the recipe's container, and gets no log — neither on the host nor inside the container. The README has told them to expect the second, so they spend the debugging effort on `docker cp` and `docker exec ls /log` before reaching the actual cause, which is the `--read-only` flag three sections earlier. The same wrong expectation is set for the Compose file, whose `read_only: true` behaves identically if a user removes the `./log` bind mount while keeping `log-file`.

## Fix

State the real failure mode and name the flag responsible:

    The standalone `docker run` recipe above mounts only `config.json`, and it
    runs `--read-only`, so `/log` is not writable at all — without the volume
    below xmrig writes no log anywhere and, per the note further down, says
    nothing about it:

Leave the `--volume "$(pwd)"/log:/log:rw` snippet that follows unchanged; it is the correct fix for both cases. The "lost on `--rm`" wording is accurate only for a writable-rootfs run, which this README does not recommend anywhere — drop it rather than qualify it.

## Resolution
README's persistent-logging paragraph now names --read-only as the reason and states the real outcome: /log is not writable at all, so xmrig writes no log anywhere and says nothing about it. The inaccurate "lost on --rm and invisible on the host" wording is gone rather than qualified — it only ever described a writable-rootfs run, which this README recommends nowhere. Confirmed against the built image that /log is a plain directory in the image layer (drwxr-xr-x xmrig root), so --read-only does cover it.
title: The persistent-logging section states the wrong failure mode for its own docker run recipe: under --read-only the log is not written to the container filesystem, it is not written at all

body:
## Problem

The comment above `ARG XMRIG_COMMIT` states: "Renovate bumps XMRIG_VERSION; the rev-parse check below then fails the build until this line is updated in the same commit." Renovate updates `XMRIG_VERSION` from the `# renovate: datasource=github-tags` annotation on the line above it. Nothing updates `XMRIG_COMMIT` — it carries no Renovate annotation, and `.github/renovate.json` adds no `customManagers`, only `extends: ["github>ivuorinen/renovate-config"]`.

The tripwire itself is sound and worth keeping. What is wrong is the sentence describing it: "in the same commit" reads as automation that exists, when the actual workflow is a red PR plus a manual edit — and the comment's `git ls-remote` recipe is not the fastest route to the value, because the build already prints it.

## Evidence

Dockerfile:2-13 —

    # renovate: datasource=github-tags depName=xmrig/xmrig
    ARG XMRIG_VERSION="v6.22.2"
    ...
    # Renovate bumps XMRIG_VERSION; the rev-parse check below
    # then fails the build until this line is updated in the same commit.
    # Refresh with:
    #   git ls-remote https://github.com/xmrig/xmrig.git 'refs/tags/<tag>^{}' 'refs/tags/<tag>'
    ARG XMRIG_COMMIT="f9e990d0f0167c92d09334213ac6950033bbbba1"

.github/renovate.json in full — no `customManagers`, no second annotation:

    {
      "$schema": "https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json",
      "extends": ["github>ivuorinen/renovate-config"]
    }

The build already emits the needed SHA, Dockerfile:43 —

    echo "upstream tag ${XMRIG_VERSION} moved: expected ${XMRIG_COMMIT}, got ${actual}"

The precedent that this repository's Renovate PRs do sit red rather than being fixed promptly: run 31063863003 (`renovate/hadolint-hadolint-action-3.x`) has been failing since 2026-08-06.

## Impact

A maintainer reading the comment expects the version and commit to move together and treats a red xmrig PR as a genuine upstream-tag-moved alarm rather than the routine second half of every bump. The `git ls-remote` recipe then sends them to a network round trip for a value the failed CI log already contains four lines above the link they clicked. Over time the plausible outcome is worse than the wasted minute: a bump PR that stays red long enough to be closed, leaving the image on an older xmrig than the repository believes it tracks.

## Fix

Rewrite the comment to describe what actually happens, and point at the value the build prints:

    # Renovate bumps XMRIG_VERSION from the annotation above; it does NOT touch
    # this line — no annotation and no customManager covers it. So every xmrig
    # bump PR is red by construction: the rev-parse check below fails, prints
    # the tag's real commit, and a maintainer pastes it here on the same branch.
    # The SHA is in the failed build log ("got <sha>"); no lookup needed. To
    # check by hand instead:
    #   git ls-remote https://github.com/xmrig/xmrig.git 'refs/tags/<tag>^{}' 'refs/tags/<tag>'

If the manual step is not acceptable, the alternative is a Renovate `customManagers` entry with `datasource=git-refs` against `https://github.com/xmrig/xmrig` capturing this line as `currentDigest`, which would let one PR carry both changes. That belongs in `.github/renovate.json` rather than the shared `ivuorinen/renovate-config` preset, since the pairing is specific to this Dockerfile.

## Resolution
The XMRIG_COMMIT comment now states what actually happens: Renovate does not touch this line, so every xmrig bump PR is red by construction, and the maintainer pastes the SHA the failed build already printed ("got <sha>") onto the same branch. The git ls-remote recipe is kept but demoted to the by-hand alternative rather than presented as the primary route. The tripwire itself is unchanged — it is the pin that holds, and the build's rev-parse check still passed on a clean local build of the current pin.
title: The XMRIG_COMMIT comment describes a same-commit Renovate update that no automation performs, so every xmrig version bump arrives as a permanently red PR
